name: Slavoj Žižek
summary: Slavoj Žižek is a Slovenian philosopher and cultural critic who writes on Hegel, Lacan and Marx, calls himself a communist, criticises both nationalist populism and liberal moralism over migration, and argues for a new universalism and a communist response to ecological and global crises.

sources.title: The Non-Existence of Norway, London Review of Books (9 September 2015)
sources.author: Slavoj Žižek
sources.usedFor: The refugee crisis: open-border advocates as hypocrites, an all-European plan, global capitalism and communism reinvented.

sources.title: We Can't Address the EU Refugee Crisis Without Confronting Global Capitalism, In These Times (2015)
sources.author: Slavoj Žižek
sources.usedFor: Refugees must respect European laws and norms; ethical universalism against both anti-immigrant brutality and uncritical tolerance.

sources.title: Until the Rich World Thinks 'One World,' Migration Will Intensify (RT interview, transcend.org, 2018)
sources.author: Slavoj Žižek
sources.usedFor: Symptomatic treatment of open borders; the need for a new universalism instead of populist nationalism.

sources.title: 'Piss Christ', Internationalism, and the Night of the World: Interview with Slavoj Žižek (Philosophy World Democracy)
sources.author: Slavoj Žižek, Kamran Baradaran and Anthony Ballas
sources.usedFor: Nationalism has no global emancipatory potential; the moralist left and open borders; China.

sources.title: After Trump's Victory: From MAGA to MEGA, e-flux Notes (November 2024)
sources.author: Slavoj Žižek
sources.usedFor: Communism needed more than ever for ecology, war and AI; the left must distance itself from the liberal centre and its 'woke corporatism'.

sources.title: Which Idea of Europe is Worth Defending?, Crisis and Critique 7(1)
sources.author: Slavoj Žižek
sources.usedFor: Europe against Trump and Putin; left populism's national sovereignty; universal solidarity.

sources.title: 'What I don't want is Western triumphalism': Slavoj Žižek on Putin's expansionism, Western complicity..., Meduza (3 February 2023)
sources.author: Slavoj Žižek
sources.usedFor: Ukraine, the EU needing more cooperative centralisation, democracy and the Yeltsin years.

sources.title: Interview with Slavoj Žižek, Philosophy Now issue 122
sources.author: Slavoj Žižek
sources.usedFor: Why communism: the commons; the era of the nation state is over; capitalism is falling apart yet most dynamic; ecology.

sources.title: Ideology isn't in the Answer, it's in the Question: An Interview with Slavoj Žižek, tripleC 18(1) (2020)
sources.author: Slavoj Žižek and Ben Gook
sources.usedFor: Fundamentalism as inherent to capitalist dynamics; the commons; Latin American populism.

sources.title: The Prospects of Radical Change Today, tripleC 16(1) (2018)
sources.author: Slavoj Žižek
sources.usedFor: Lenin's State and Revolution and Stalinism; the revolutionary subject; elections and the people; class struggle and immigration; human rights as basic material rights; Europe's emancipatory core.

sources.title: In the Wake of Paris Attacks the Left Must Embrace Its Radical Western Roots, In These Times (16 November 2015)
sources.author: Slavoj Žižek
sources.usedFor: Minimum norms for all (religious freedom, individual freedom against group pressure, women's rights), limits on free movement, gay and women's rights, class struggle and global solidarity.

sources.title: Pacifism is the wrong response to the war in Ukraine, The Guardian (21 June 2022), standfirst and opening, as reposted on Pipedot
sources.author: Slavoj Žižek
sources.usedFor: 'The least we owe Ukraine is full support, and to do this we need a stronger Nato'; pacifists remain caught in their own version of 'imagine'.

sources.title: Žižek, Slavoj, Internet Encyclopedia of Philosophy
sources.author: Internet Encyclopedia of Philosophy
sources.usedFor: Scholarly account of his political philosophy, used to check the reading.

notFound.work: His books (Violence, Living in the End Times, Trouble in Paradise, Pandemic!) and Guardian columns

notes: First audit. Read in full: his LRB essay on the refugee crisis (2015), In These Times piece, the RT interview, an interview in Philosophy World Democracy, an e-flux essay of 2024, a Crisis and Critique paper on Europe, and the Internet Encyclopedia of Philosophy entry. His essays use provocation and irony, so only passages stating a position are used. Searched without a settled answer: capitalism and planning, democracy, revolution and violence, religion, gender, the state, ecology and climate, nationalism and populism. The tripleC interview (Ben Gook, 2020) and a Meduza interview (2023) were also read; Project Syndicate columns are open only as excerpts ('register to continue') and are not used; the Peterson debate has no open full transcript; the Philosophical Salon pages found are commentary by others, not his own text; the Conversations with Tyler transcript refused automated access (403) and was not retried. Nothing read gives a position on most statements; they stay null. YouTube and MediaSum hold no transcripts of him (MediaSum: none).
